predecessors.name: Tang dynasty
predecessors.text: Shanxi without the Linfen, Hezhong and Jincheng commands that Later Liang held

successors.name: Later Tang
successors.text: the 922 Jin without the Zhaoyi circuit

ledger.x: 907: with the Tang gone, Li Keyong's Jin holds Shanxi from Taiyuan.
913: Li Cunxu's Jin conquers Liu Shouguang's Yan.
916: the north bank of the Yellow River goes to Jin.

923: the Jin becomes the Later Tang (Tongguang era from 13 May 923) and the war goes on under that name until the fall of Kaifeng, which the later-liang-dynasty dossier dates to 19 November 923 and the later-tang dossier carries.

wars.name: Jin conquest of Yan
wars.outcome: Zhou besieged You Prefecture by summer 913; Liu Shouguang fled, was captured and the Yan was destroyed (the Yan page ends it in 914).

wars.name: Jin-Later Liang war
wars.outcome: Jin took Tianxiong (915) and nearly all Later Liang land north of the Yellow River by fall 916, crossed to Yangliu in 917, fought a drawn battle at Huliu Slope (919), lost Wei Prefecture (921-922) and Zhaoyi (spring 923); Li Cunxu proclaimed the Tang in 923…

wars.name: Jin conquest of Zhao
wars.outcome: After Wang Rong was killed in a mutiny in 921, Jin besieged Zhenzhou and starved Zhang into capitulation in 922; Zhao's territory was incorporated into Jin.

certainty.note: The Jin realm is known by circuits and prefectures; the Yellow River line after 916 is the best-known frontier but no treaty fixes it.
